title: Japan's Companies Rank Lowest for AI Satisfaction
paragraphs: Many companies around the world are using artificial intelligence to work faster and save money. But according to a new survey, Japanese companies are the least happy with the results.

The survey was carried out by PwC Japan, part of the international consulting company PwC. In February and March 2026, it asked about 3,000 managers in six countries: Japan, the United States, the United Kingdom, Germany, China and South Korea. The managers worked at large companies with yearly sales of at least 50 billion yen.

The managers were asked if AI had been more useful than they expected. In Japan, only 9% said that AI had exceeded their expectations. This was the lowest result of all six countries. In comparison, the figure was 38% in the United States and 32% in the United Kingdom. It was 18% in China, 17% in Germany and 11% in South Korea. In Japan, 47% of managers said AI had met their expectations.

There was also a big difference in who benefits from AI. In the US and the UK, more than 70% of managers said that the benefits of AI were reaching customers and employees. In Japan, the figure was only around 40%.

One reason may be the way Japanese companies use AI. According to the survey, they mainly use it for simple tasks, such as writing reports and emails. These tasks can save some time, but they may not bring big changes to a business.
Other research also shows that Japan is slower to use AI. For example, in a survey for the Reuters news agency in 2026, only 16% of Japanese companies said they used AI across their whole company.

Experts warn that if Japanese companies are slow to use AI, it could be harder for the country to reach its goal of making companies more productive. Still, in the Reuters survey, no companies said they planned to spend less money on AI in the next one to two years.
